name: L-Arginine ethyl ester

lead: L-arginine ethyl ester is arginine with an ethyl group attached. It is sold in pump-style supplements for lifters who want better muscle fullness and vascularity.
In the lab, related arginine esters are mainly used as test reagents.

paras: Arginine is the raw material for nitric oxide, which widens blood vessels. The ester form is marketed as more absorbable than plain arginine.
No human safety or effectiveness studies of the ethyl ester as a supplement were found. Laboratory research covers other uses.

chain: Arginine form taken as a supplement
Claimed to raise nitric oxide and blood flow
Fuller muscle pumps and a more vascular look during training
angle.text: Lifters use arginine products hoping for stronger pumps and vascularity. The ethyl ester is marketed as a more absorbable form of the same idea.

lead: L-arginine ethyl ester (AEE) is the ethyl ester form of the amino acid L-arginine. It is sold as a supplement ingredient in the muscle and pump category, where users take it hoping that arginine's role as a nitric oxide precursor will support blood flow and a fuller, more vascular look during training. [1]

The ester form is chemically more lipophilic than plain arginine, which is the reason given by marketers for choosing it. In laboratory research, arginine ethyl ester appears mostly as a reagent: a close relative, benzoyl-arginine ethyl ester (BAEE), is a standard substrate for measuring protease activity. [2][3]
Research on AEE itself in humans for physique or appearance is not found in the sources reviewed; published work covers laboratory and cell models. [4]

paras: In supplement marketing, arginine esters are positioned for muscle pumps and training performance. The reasoning is that arginine is the substrate for nitric oxide synthesis, a vasodilating signal. [1]

The compound is the ethyl ester of arginine. Related esters are widely used in the laboratory: benzoyl-arginine ethyl ester is a classic enzyme substrate for trypsin, papain and related proteases, and lauroyl arginine ethyl ester is used as a food preservative. [2][3][5]
No studies found. Laboratory work has shown arginine ethyl ester suppressing polyglutamine protein aggregation in cell, yeast and fruit fly models of Huntington's disease. [4]
Safety data on arginine ethyl ester as an oral supplement were not found in the sources reviewed; arginine products carry the usual supplement label guidance.
